assumptions: The packet's cited Polish and EU legal findings are accurate, but final contract design and regulated activities will be reviewed by qualified Polish counsel.
The initial service targets qualifying B2B commercial transactions and screens for performed obligations, complete evidence, debtor solvency, and undisputed amounts before intervention.
Court, enforcement, and any other reserved legal work is performed by appropriately licensed external partners rather than the founder company.
Recovered funds can be routed directly to creditors or through a counsel-approved payment structure so client-money custody is not essential to the model.
The founder keeps the corporate job, contributes no more than five hours per day, and uses automation and partners rather than personally running a call center or litigation practice.
Missing pilots, contracts, and commercial metrics are treated as material uncertainty at the planning stage, not as proof of zero demand or impossible economics.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A narrow-sector pilot cohort should show signed portfolio mandates, creditor retention and debtor-relationship outcomes, recovery rate and time-to-cash versus incumbents, fully loaded contribution margin by claim, repeatable accountant-channel CAC and referral economics, and retained Polish counsel plus partner agreements validating authority, fees, data rights, escalation, liability, and payment flows.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Late B2B invoices create a measurable loss and, when statutory conditions are met, calculable interest and recovery-cost rights. Combining evidence checks, dated calculations, workflow automation, and outcome-based pricing is coherent, but it is an optimization of an established collection model rather than a demonstrated market misunderstanding or unique control mechanism.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Late payment is frequent, costly, and time-consuming, and incumbent success-fee services establish that some creditors pay for recovery. However, creditors' documented fear of damaging customer relationships weakens the statutory-interest wedge, while willingness to grant exclusivity, accept the proposed fee split, and renew remains untested rather than disproven.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Contingency pricing aligns incentives, removes an upfront-budget objection, and has credible market price anchors. Attractive owner economics are nevertheless uncertain because recoverability, dispute labor, partner and court costs, channel share, CAC, support and compliance overhead, and time to cleared cash have not been measured together; the illustrative wealth path also requires very large administered principal.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Official evidence supports a large Polish corporate-claims market and substantial recurring late-payment pain. The proposed beachhead—Polish SMEs with recurring undisputed B2B delays—is still broad and not tied to a narrow sector with standardized proof, predictable collectability, or privileged access, making an efficient initial win less clear.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Established collectors already offer online invoice upload, success fees, amicable collection, tracking, and legal escalation, and one is embedded directly in accounting software. The entrant has no evidenced recovery uplift, cost advantage, proprietary channel, specialist vertical position, or enforceable control that would support dominance.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A trusted receivables workflow could expand into payment-risk scoring, cash-flow forecasting, pre-due interventions, financing referrals, additional creditor segments, or nearby EU markets. Those adjacencies are plausible, but they depend on customer trust, lawful reusable-data rights, and distribution that the current structure has not yet secured.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: The proposed 12-month exclusive mandate does not provide the claimed durable control: authority is generally revocable and a mandate-like contract may be terminable at any time. Claim ownership remains with the creditor, litigation depends on qualified representatives, and GDPR and contract constraints prevent assuming a cross-client data moat.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Transparent calculations, evidence completeness, and accountant-native onboarding could improve convenience, but the packet does not establish a material advantage over incumbents that already combine software handoff, tracking, customer decision control, contingency pricing, and escalation. The contemplated differentiation is currently feature-level and imitable.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Persistent late-payment pressure, high current statutory rates, and AI-enabled document and workflow automation are favorable. Against that, collection is a mature and well-served market, and the packet identifies no regulatory or channel transition that uniquely advantages a new entrant now.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Accountants and bookkeepers are a sensible trust-based route, and an incumbent integration proves the route can work. No partner has committed referrals, integrations, economics, or exclusivity for this entrant, while incumbents already control embedded channels and creditor acquisition likely requires trust-heavy selling incompatible with effortless part-time scale.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A low-capital pilot and substantial automation fit the founder's analytical skills, and licensed partners can cover reserved work. Execution still combines Polish contract and representation boundaries, GDPR, evidence exceptions, disputes, complaints, reconciliation, partner management, and long collection cycles; there is no evidence yet that these operations fit a five-hour daily limit at scale.

highest_value_structural_change: Replace revocable creditor-level exclusivity as the moat with a multi-year embedded distribution and data-rights agreement with a bookkeeping or ERP platform serving one evidence-standardized vertical, entering the workflow before default and combining a subscription with success fees; this would create controlled acquisition, richer lawful data, and a clearer performance advantage.
main_structural_strength: The service attaches outcome-based pricing to a recurring, objectively measurable cash-flow problem, with statutory calculations and evidence triage that are amenable to automation and can be piloted without large upfront capital.
primary_score_limiter: There is no durable, founder-controlled advantage over established collectors: the central exclusive mandate is externally controlled and the claimed data and distribution moats lack contractual or commercial support.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Close incumbents already provide the proposed core workflow—including online intake, contingency fees, tracking, amicable collection, accounting-software integration, and legal escalation—while Polish mandate and authority rules make the candidate's supposed 12-month for-cause-only exclusive control revocable or terminable.
